project_name: Diagrams as Code - Directed IIoT Engine

can_render_without_graphviz.details: Renders high-fidelity SVG diagrams directly using pure Python standard library string formatting without external Graphviz, Cairo, or binary dependencies.

can_position_shapes_relatively.details: Directional placement (right_of, left_of, below, above) with margin padding and alignment constraints resolved via iterative topological DAG solver.

can_position_shapes_with_unit_basis.details: Normalized coordinate placement across 0.0-1.0 unit-basis or percentage strings ('50%', '25%') mapped to canvas dimensions.

can_decouple_shape_definition_from_locat.details: Complete decoupling of shape instantiation, existence, and spatial placement. Shapes can be defined unplaced, placed late, relocated, or cloned from prototypes.

can_generate_living_bom_documentation.details: Extracts diagram inventory, group affiliations, connection topology, and technical metadata into Markdown tables and JSON catalogs.

can_draw_sequence_diagrams.details: Participants, messages, replies, self-calls, activations, notes and loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break frames, laid out from the events with the standard library alone.

can_draw_gantt_charts_and_timelines.details: Tasks with dependencies and lag, phases, milestones, progress and a computed critical path; dated events with non-overlapping labels.

has_auto_layout.details: A deterministic layered engine places unpinned shapes and groups from the edge structure (direction LR or TB); pinned shapes coexist via .at()/.right_of(), and a LayoutWarning flags any pin that overlaps an auto-placed sibling.

can_route_cubic_bezier_curves.details: Pure-Python analytical cubic Bezier edge routing with outward cardinal normal port tangents, distance-proportional tension scaling, native SVG M...C path rendering, and physical arc-length midpoint protocol badge placement.

can_round_orthogonal_corners.details: Quadratic Bezier corner filleting for orthogonal edges with dynamic 50% segment budget clamping, 2.0px suppression threshold, obstacle apex clearance guard, and native SVG Q commands.

capabilities.name: Core Geometry and Unit-Basis Coordinate Engine
capabilities.details: Immutable 2D geometric primitives, 9-point cardinal/intercardinal rect anchors, rect expansion/union, and normalized canvas unit-basis coordinate conversion.

capabilities.name: Decoupled Elements and Iterative DAG Constraint Solver
capabilities.details: Directed shape-to-shape relative positioning (right_of, left_of, below, above) with alignment and margin padding. Evaluates dependency DAGs with cycle detection and unconstrained element retention.

capabilities.name: Hierarchical Grouping, Auto-Bounding, and Group Flow
capabilities.details: Hierarchical container elements with bottom-up recursive auto-bounding, child coordinate delta propagation, cycle prevention, and group-to-group flow placement.

capabilities.name: Orthogonal Manhattan Routing and Port Deduction
capabilities.details: Intelligent edge connection model with automatic port deduction (North, South, East, West), orthogonal Manhattan waypoints calculation, and collinear straight-line simplification.

capabilities.name: Obstacle-Aware Orthogonal Routing and Multi-Rank Layout
capabilities.details: Segment-box collision detection with clearance corridors, shortest Manhattan detour channel routing around intermediate obstacles, and multi-rank crossing minimization via virtual dummy vertices.

capabilities.name: Cubic Bezier Edge Routing and SVG Path Generation
capabilities.details: Pure-Python analytical cubic Bezier edge routing (Routing.CURVE). Computes outward cardinal normal port tangents, distance-proportional handle heuristics, native SVG M...C path rendering with tangentially aligned destination arrowheads, and physical arc-length midpoint protocol badge positioning.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_geometry.py tests/test_routing.py tests/test_renderer_svg.py -k "curve or bezier"

capabilities.name: Rounded Corner Fillets for Orthogonal Routing
capabilities.details: Quadratic Bezier corner filleting for orthogonal Manhattan edges (corner_radius and arc_radius alias on Edge and Diagram). Emits native SVG Q commands with dynamic 50% segment budget clamping, straight port lead-in preservation, 2.0px threshold suppression, and obstacle clearance apex guards.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_geometry.py tests/test_routing.py tests/test_renderer_svg.py -k "fillet or corner_radius"

capabilities.name: Vector Theming Engine and Vector Shape Library
capabilities.details: 13 theme presets (8 dark, 4 light, 1 high-contrast), 60 built-in vector icons across 8 domains, dynamic icon loading from SVG files/directories, and standalone SVG vector primitives.

capabilities.name: Multi-Domain Reference Topologies & Automated Test Suite
capabilities.details: 143 executable domain reference diagrams across cloud, ai, computer, datacenter, business_process, cybersecurity, network_engineering, iiot, database, enterprise_architecture, manufacturing, mind_map, and computer_science demonstrating multi-theme styling, BOM generation, and automated test verification. Twelve newer galleries add 114 more (agentic_dev, semiconductor, chemistry, data_engineering, ml_models, devops, biology, chemical_engineering, org, electronics at 10 each; sequence 3; project_management 11), for 361 example scripts in all.

capabilities.name: Auto-Layout Engine and Editable Layout File
capabilities.details: Deterministic Sugiyama-style ranked placement (layout="auto", direction LR or TB) for unpinned shapes and groups scope by scope; an editable JSON layout file keyed by explicit id= or label path (diagrams-as-code layout export); pinned shapes and relative placement coexist with auto-placed siblings, with a LayoutWarning raised on overlap.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_layout_layered.py tests/test_layout_graph.py tests/test_layout_pipeline.py tests/test_layout_sidecar.py

capabilities.name: The diagrams-as-code Command
capabilities.details: Entrypoint diagrams-as-code (also python -m diagrams_as_code) with subcommands render, lint, layout export, mcp, themes, icons, api, examples and source; batch-renders scripts or directories to SVG/PNG/BOM, exports layout files, and lists built-in themes and icons. Machine interface: `--json` on `render`, `lint`, `themes` and `icons` prints exactly one JSON document on stdout (diagnostics and any script `print` go to stderr); `api [NAME]` lists the public Python API with signatures and summaries (the same data as the MCP `describe_api`), `examples [--domain D]` lists the gallery, `source EXAMPLE` prints an example script. Lint JSON carries file, kind, detail and the ids of the elements involved. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 findings or failures, 2 usage error.

capabilities.name: Pure-Python Zero-Binary SVG Vector Renderer
capabilities.details: Produces valid, standalone W3C SVG XML documents featuring responsive viewBox scaling, arrowhead markers, drop shadow filters, ordered group rendering, and automated luminance contrast text coloring.

capabilities.name: Fluent Diagram Context Manager and Operator Syntax
capabilities.details: Pythonic context manager with bitshift connection operator overloading (s1 >> s2, s1 >> diag.edge(...) >> s2, fan-in/fan-out lists), automatic group scoping, decoupled shape lifecycles, and prototype cloning.

capabilities.name: Living Documentation & Bill of Materials (BOM) Engine
capabilities.details: Extracts diagram inventory, parent groups, connection routes, and technical metadata into Markdown tables and JSON catalogs, with automated README.md synchronization.

capabilities.name: Interactive SVG Pan-Zoom and Collapsible Groups
capabilities.details: Pure-Python client-side interactive SVG generation with zero external runtime dependencies. Features responsive click-drag viewport panning, cursor-anchored mouse wheel zoom, viewport reset HUD controls, and interactive collapsible groups with header toggles and recursive visibility propagation.

capabilities.name: CLI Interactive Export Option
capabilities.details: Command-line flags (--interactive, --no-interactive) for diagrams-as-code render and batch directory exports to emit responsive, pan/zoom-enabled SVG assets directly.

capabilities.name: Client-Side Search and Node Highlighting
capabilities.details: Client-side search input field integrated directly into the HUD controls. Dynamically matches node labels and IDs, dimming non-matching elements and highlighting matches in real-time.

capabilities.name: Viewport Minimap Overview and Drag Navigation
capabilities.details: Pinned overview minimap thumbnail widget rendered in the bottom-right corner of interactive SVG canvases, featuring responsive visible bounds rectangle and smooth drag navigation.

capabilities.name: Obstacle Detection and Deflection for Curved Edges
capabilities.details: Two-tier collision detection combining bounding box broadphase filtering with recursive De Casteljau subdivision, automatic reverse-flow lateral port resolution and escape routing, and adaptive C1-continuous spline deflection waypoints around intervening obstacles.

capabilities.name: Technical Drawing Primitives
capabilities.details: Free text, captions and brackets; polygons, polylines and SVG paths; dashed layer bands with side notes; shapes nested in shapes and double borders; edge stroke weight, seven arrowhead styles, two-way arrows and ellipsis connectors; edge ends at fractional side anchors or bare points, shared-trunk fan-out, leaders and splines through given points; convex solids in oblique and isometric projection with hidden-edge dashing, translucent faces and cutting planes; z-order; align(), distribute(), grid snap and px/pt/mm lengths. Nine focused figures in examples/primitives.

capabilities.name: Technical Figures, Lint and Golden Images
capabilities.details: Eleven paper-style figures in examples/technical, the first a reproduction of a reference figure; `diagrams-as-code lint` reports visual defects by name and exits 1 if any are found; golden-image regression tests compare every technical figure with a stored picture, rendered with pinned fonts so results match across machines; a technical-figures guide and a math markup reference.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_technical_examples.py tests/test_golden_images.py tests/test_lint.py && uv run diagrams-as-code lint examples

capabilities.name: Plot Kit and Textbook Galleries
capabilities.details: Data-space plotting on a Diagram with the standard library alone: axes with ticks, grid, linear and log mapping, function and parametric curves clipped to the window and broken at asymptotes, tangents, shaded areas and bands, Riemann rectangles, slope and vector fields, RK4 trajectories and ODE solutions, candlesticks, stacked and plain bar charts, legends, orbits with direction arrows, custom tick labels and decade log ticks. Math markup gains bars, roots and more function names. Fifty textbook figures in examples/calculus_math, differential_equations, physics, finance and logic.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_plot.py tests/test_textbook_examples.py && uv run diagrams-as-code lint examples

capabilities.name: Drafting Kit and Medical, Engineering, CAD Galleries
capabilities.details: Drafting and anatomy primitives with the standard library alone: dimension lines, radius and diameter leaders, even-odd section hatching with holes, centerlines, hidden lines, section arrows, GD&T frames, smooth organic outlines, leaders and ECG-style traces. Thirty figures in examples/medical, engineering and cad.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_draft.py tests/test_clinical_engineering_examples.py && uv run diagrams-as-code lint examples

capabilities.name: Vector PDF Export
capabilities.details: One-page vector PDF written with the standard library alone, at 0.75 pt per px, drawn from the SVG the renderer writes so the two match: paths, fills, dashes, arrowheads, opacity, text and math. Text uses the standard PDF fonts with nothing embedded; math is outlines; drop shadows are approximated with translucent rings. `diagrams-as-code render --format pdf` writes it from the command line.

capabilities.name: MCP Server
capabilities.details: A stdlib-only JSON-RPC 2.0 server over stdio (MCP revision 2025-06-18), started with `diagrams-as-code mcp [--root DIR]`. Tools: list_examples, render, lint, render_source, lint_source, get_example, list_domains, describe_api, capabilities, list_themes, list_icons. Beyond file-based `render` and `lint`, `render_source` and `lint_source` take script text, so a client with no file-write tool can create a diagram (the SVG comes back inline, bounded at 100,000 characters with a `truncated` flag, and/or is written under `out` inside the root); `get_example`, `list_domains`, `describe_api` and `capabilities` let an agent discover what exists. Source text runs as arbitrary Python in the same sandbox. Every tool declares an `inputSchema` (descriptions, enums) and, for object results, an `outputSchema`; failures are structured as `{error: {code, message, line?}}` with a stable code (`invalid_argument`, `path_outside_root`, `not_found`, `no_scripts`, `script_error`, `timeout`, `resource_limit`, `sandbox_failure`, `output_error`, `internal_error`). Script and output paths are confined to --root (symlinks re-resolved, script-chosen output names must be plain stems), messages are size-capped, malformed input never ends the session, and errors do not leak absolute paths. Each script runs in a resource-limited child process (sandbox.py): wall-clock timeout (--timeout, default 60 s, process group killed), CPU and memory caps on POSIX (--memory-mb, default 2048; address space is only enforced on Linux), stdin closed, stdout discarded, stderr capped, scrubbed environment. This limits resources and protects the protocol stream; it is not file or network isolation, so for untrusted scripts also run the server in a container.

capabilities.name: TeX-like Math Markup in Labels and Captions
capabilities.details: Frac, binom, sqrt with an index (sqrt[n]{x}), the accents hat, widehat, tilde, widetilde, dot, ddot, vec and grave, the equilibrium signs rightleftharpoons and rightleftarrows (two stacked arrows, not harpoons), and \ce{H2O} for chemical formulas with computed subscripts and charges. acute, check and breve are unsupported (no outlines) and raise MathError. Reference: docs/math-markup.md.

capabilities.name: UML Sequence Diagram Kit
capabilities.details: Participants, synchronous, asynchronous and reply messages, self-calls, activation bars, notes and loop, alt, opt, par, critical and break frames, placed by a computed layout with the standard library alone. Draws onto an ordinary Diagram, so themes, lint, SVG, PNG and PDF apply. Horizontal messages only; no lost/found messages, create/destroy or ref frames. Three examples in examples/sequence; guide: docs/sequence-diagrams.md.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_sequence.py tests/test_domain_examples.py && uv run diagrams-as-code lint examples/sequence

capabilities.name: Gantt Chart and Timeline Kit
capabilities.details: GanttChart schedules tasks from durations and finish-to-start dependencies with lag, groups them in phases, draws milestones, percent done and a status line, and computes and highlights the critical path with orthogonal dependency arrows. Timeline places dated events on a ruler with labels stacked so none overlap. Calendar days only; about 0.5% of arrows on dense random charts can be unroutable (a warning is raised). Eleven examples in examples/project_management; guide: docs/gantt-timelines.md.
capabilities.verification: uv run pytest tests/test_gantt.py tests/test_domain_examples.py && uv run diagrams-as-code lint examples/project_management
